objective_summary: COMPLETED, with one same-run logic-bug repair cycle -- a real, live, controlled and disclosed planted-defect demonstration of the harness's bounded same-run Quality-Engineer logic-failure route-back loop (task T-LATEFEE2; see also the earlier, related attempt run-20260805-latefee-004, closed 'blocked' on an unrelated transport-repair budget issue before Verification was ever reached). Discovery and Research completed cleanly: scope.json (transparently disclosing that the first implementation pass is designed to satisfy AC-1 but not AC-2) and findings.json (a real, live-dispatched Architect, agent ad917d57f05959c2d, 8 found + 1 inferred; one transport-only correction for an invalid-JSON trailing comma) were validated and promoted. Implementation: a real, live-dispatched Engineer (agent a7ec78b1632a775ed) wrote a genuine failing TDD test first for the first pass (independently confirmed via git status/diff -- only the in-scope test file changed before command C-1), implemented per the disclosed literal-policy-document boundary as directed, and its report was promoted as implementation-report.json (status ready_for_verification). Verification: a real, live-dispatched Quality Engineer (agent a476bba2ae25e5638) independently ran the Engineer's own AC-1 tests (V-1, pass) and then independently discovered and ran the pre-existing, out-of-scope regression fixture for AC-2 (V-2), which genuinely failed (exit_code 1, AssertionError: assert 'standard' == 'severe' at day 30) -- a real logic_bug, promoted as verification-report.json with final_verdict 'fail' and routed_back_to_engineer.routed true. The genuine logic_bug was routed back to the exact same Engineer agent id via SendMessage, carrying the real, unredacted Quality Engineer failure evidence; the Engineer re-applied TDD (updating its own in-scope regression test first, under a fresh command id C-3, confirmed failing for the expected reason before any production edit), then made the smallest corrective edit (one comparison operator, `<= 30` to `< 30`) and confirmed the fix (C-4, exit_code 0, 4 passed including the previously-failing regression fixture). The repair round's implementation report was promoted separately as implementation-report.repair-1.json, leaving the original implementation-report.json retained and untouched. The exact same Quality Engineer agent was then resumed via SendMessage for re-verification: it re-ran AC-1 (V-3, pass) and AC-2 (V-4, pass) with fresh command ids, and its repair-round report was promoted separately as verification-report.repair-1.json (final_verdict 'pass', routed_back_to_engineer.routed false), leaving the original verification-report.json retained and untouched. The orchestrator independently re-verified this repaired pass rather than trusting the Quality Engineer's word alone: re-ran the narrow scope through the real, forked test-runner Skill (ORCH-1, exit_code 0) and the full demo-repo suite (ORCH-2, exit_code 0, 106 passed -- the prior 102-test baseline plus 4 new tests across the Engineer's own test file and the pre-existing regression fixture), with check_command_identity explicitly run and matched for every staged command (C-1..C-4, V-1..V-4) and both ORCH-* commands, per Standing rule 13. git status/diff independently confirmed exactly four new demo-repo files across the whole session (demo-repo/docs/late-fee-tier-policy.md, demo-repo/src/loanflow/late_fee_tier.py, demo-repo/tests/unit/test_late_fee_tier.py, demo-repo/tests/unit/test_late_fee_tier_regression.py) -- no existing file modified, no out-of-scope or Protected Path file touched. Exactly one Architect, one Engineer, and one Quality Engineer dispatch occurred for this run (agent_dispatch policy events with dispatch_sequence 1 each); every subsequent turn was a SendMessage resume of that same agent id, never a replacement agent. Two transport-only corrections occurred and were each resolved within their one-per-phase budget: one for Research (an invalid-JSON trailing comma) and one for the Implementation phase's repair-cycle finalization_evidence_requested turn (leading prose) -- both retained as transport_parse_failure policy events, both repaired via the documented protocol, neither weakened.
remaining_risks: A related, earlier attempt for this same demonstration (run-20260805-latefee-004) closed 'blocked': its Engineer produced two independently Markdown-fenced replies within one Implementation phase, exhausting the one-correction-per-phase transport-repair budget on the first and blocking on the second. This run's Engineer dispatch included an explicit caller_note reminder about raw-JSON-only replies, which correlated with cleaner transport behavior in round 1 (zero transport failures) though the repair round still needed one correction -- this is suggestive, not proof of causation.

A genuine, narrow gap in harness/orchestrator/live_cli.py's Option C live bridge was found and worked around, not fixed: its `promote_artifact` operation always targets the single canonical filename per phase (evidence_io.CANONICAL_FILENAMES) and has no parameter for a repair-round alternate filename, so calling it a second time for the 'implementation'/'verification' phase correctly refuses (EvidenceCollisionError) rather than overwriting the original -- confirmed live in this run. Both repair-round artifacts (implementation-report.repair-1.json, verification-report.repair-1.json) were instead promoted via a direct call to the same underlying evidence_io.promote_canonical() function core.py itself uses for this exact purpose, after independently validating each via the real validate_artifact operation first -- no validation was skipped or weakened, but this is a bridge-tooling gap that should be closed in live_cli.py itself in a future milestone rather than worked around by direct calls every time.

Two real command_result runs of the full demo-repo suite in this session (this run's ORCH-2, and the standalone `python -m pytest demo-repo/tests -q` re-run performed for the final report) both show 106 passed -- the repair round changed no test count from what the first (buggy) pass had already added; only the boundary behavior itself changed between the first pass and the repair.
follow_up_actions: Add a repair-round filename parameter to harness/orchestrator/live_cli.py's promote_artifact operation (e.g. an optional `canonical_filename` field) so future live repair cycles do not need a direct evidence_io.promote_canonical() call outside the live_cli bridge.

Consider whether the Engineer's real, recurring tendency to wrap replies in Markdown fences or add leading prose (observed across both run-20260805-latefee-004 and this run) warrants a stronger, more explicit no-fence/no-prose reminder built into engineer.md itself, rather than relying on a caller-supplied ad hoc caller_note each dispatch.

Retire or clearly relabel the demo-repo/docs/late-fee-tier-policy.md and test_late_fee_tier_regression.py fixture files as historical demonstration evidence (not a real product feature) if late_fee_tier.py is ever extended for a real purpose.
